author: Roman Strokov
description: Diagnostic Atlas: 60 observable criteria for 12 dimensions × 5 levels
changelog_note: Atlas criteria unchanged from v1.0. Spin glass analogy added to book text §4.7 only.

Z.name: Identity
Z.description: How the system understands itself, its past, and its future

levels.0: No shared conceptual apparatus. Groups use different terms for the same processes. Mutual incomprehension.
levels.1: Terms are understood. Participants can read a document of the other side. But do not use the shared language in everyday speech.
levels.2: Shared language is used in working documents. Meetings are conducted in the shared language. Terms do not require explanation.
levels.3: Shared language is used for joint problem-solving. New terms are created jointly. Language adapts to new tasks.
levels.4: Language is generated by the system independently. New concepts emerge organically, without external impulse. Language becomes an environment, not a tool.

levels.0: No awareness of role. The element does not understand why it is in the system.
levels.1: Execution by protocol. The element acts by instruction, does not initiate.
levels.2: Initiative within the task. The element adapts actions to the situation.
levels.3: Independent decision-making. The element acts as a subject, not an object.
levels.4: Agenda-setting. The element generates directions, reproduces agency.

levels.0: No vision. The system does not formulate where it is going.
levels.1: Vision is formulated by one center. Not shared. Transmitted from above.
levels.2: Vision is discussed. Participants understand the direction but do not influence it.
levels.3: Vision is shared. Participants adjust the direction jointly.
levels.4: Vision is generated by the system. New directions emerge organically.

Y.name: Quality
Y.description: What the system creates and how it is embedded in the environment

levels.0: What is created does not exist in everyday life. A project on paper. No use.
levels.1: Formal integration. Protocol is signed. Procedure exists. But is not used in everyday practice.
levels.2: Use in everyday life. Participants turn to what is created without compulsion. Embedded in routine.
levels.3: Self-reproduction. What is created is updated by participants without external impulse. The procedure lives, not merely exists.
levels.4: Generation of new. Participants create new formats based on what is embedded. Embeddedness becomes a source of innovation.

levels.0: No accounting for needs. What is created does not correspond to the environment.
levels.1: Formal accounting. Needs are recorded but do not influence the result.
levels.2: Substantive accounting. What is created is adapted to key needs.
levels.3: Deep adaptation. What is created accounts for hidden needs, unformulated.
levels.4: Joint adaptation. Environment and what is created adapt to each other.

levels.0: No new formats. The system reproduces the existing.
levels.1: New formats are proposed from outside. The system does not generate.
levels.2: New formats emerge inside but do not take root.
levels.3: New formats emerge and are embedded. The system renews.
levels.4: New formats are generated continuously. Innovation becomes the norm.

X.name: Connections
X.description: Structure of links between elements of the system

levels.0: No channels. Elements are not connected.
levels.1: One channel. Interaction through a single intermediary.
levels.2: Several independent channels. Interaction does not depend on one intermediary.
levels.3: Channels cover the majority of elements. The network is dense.
levels.4: Channels are generated independently. New connections emerge without external impulse.

levels.0: No interaction. Groups do not know each other. Channel is absent.
levels.1: Interaction by protocol. Request — response. Formal. Outside the protocol, no contacts.
levels.2: Consultation. One side helps the other formulate a task. Exchange is substantive, not formal.
levels.3: Joint decision-making. Sides defend each other before third parties. The boundary 'us — them' is blurred.
levels.4: Exchange of strategic information. Joint risk management. Sides act as a single subject.

levels.0: No interaction. Channels exist but are not used.
levels.1: Interaction is rare, on request. Reactive.
levels.3: Interaction is continuous. Without schedule, by need.
levels.4: Interaction generates new occasions. The flow creates itself.

W.name: Resources
W.description: Realized connection through resources — volume, resilience, temporal structure

levels.1: Exchange through one center. All flows through one channel.
levels.2: Exchange through several channels. Share of non-central channels grows.
levels.3: Exchange is diversified. No dependence on one source.
levels.4: Exchange generates new flows. Resources are attracted independently.

levels.0: No exchange. No dependence. No resilience.
levels.1: Exchange through one channel. Upon loss of the channel, exchange stops. The system does not withstand loss.
levels.2: Exchange through several channels. Upon loss of one channel, exchange continues but with delay. The system adapts.
levels.3: Exchange is resilient to loss of a key element. The system restructures without external intervention.
levels.4: Exchange generates new channels independently. The system expands without external impulse. Resilience becomes a source of growth.

levels.3: Long-term commitments. Horizon — years. Joint planning.
levels.4: Open-ended commitments. The system reproduces commitments independently.

synchronization.within_axis: Spread ≤ 1. Axis is synchronized. Spread ≥ 2 — internal desynchronization, priority to lagging dimension.
synchronization.between_axes: Spread between means ≤ 1. System is synchronized. Spread ≥ 2 — inter-axis desynchronization, priority to lagging axis.

rules.field_separation: Z, Y, X — action field. W — result field. Do not manage W directly. W will follow.
rules.transition_pattern: Z → Y/X → W. Identity first. Resources last. Observed regularity, not a recommendation.
rules.weak_link: The minimum determines reality. Axis with values 3, 1, 3 operates at level 1, not 2.33.

zones.growth: Z, Y, X grow. W lags. Potential is accumulated. Do not force W.
zones.risk: W grows. Z, Y, X lag. Resources without structure. Urgent actions on Z, Y, X.
zones.stagnation: Levels do not change 3+ cycles. Diagnostics: ceiling or lack of effort.
zones.false_wellbeing: W holds. Z, Y, X fall. Resources exist, structure is destroyed. Urgent.
